To fix (2)

To fix Exact P-Values

What we found

We found 1 imprecise p value out of 15 detected p values.

Show details

Reporting p values imprecisely (e.g., p < .05) reduces transparency, reproducibility, and re-use (e.g., in p value meta-analyses). Best practice is to report exact p-values with three decimal places (e.g., p = .032) unless p values are smaller than 0.001, in which case you can use p < .001.

This module sometimes flags false positives when sentences discuss how p-value thresholds were set. It can also miss an imprecise p-value that is reported against a threshold (e.g., “decreased at the p < .05 significance threshold”).

P-Value Text
p < 0.05 Bold pvalues indicate statistical significance (p < 0.05 after class-wise FDR adjustment).

The APA manual states: Report exact p values (e.g., p = .031) to two or three decimal places. However, report p values less than .001 as p < .001. However, 2 decimals is too imprecise for many use-cases (e.g., a p value meta-analysis), so report p values with three digits.

American Psychological Association (2020). Publication manual of the American Psychological Association, 7 edition. American Psychological Association.

To fix Codebook Check

What we found

We found no codebook or README documentation for the 778 extracted data columns.

Show details

This module checks whether each extracted data column is documented in a codebook or README, and flags documented variables that never appear in the data.

We examined 2 codebook/README/label sources and 778 data columns across 46 files.

No codebook or README documentation was found, so no data columns could be matched to variable definitions.

To check (4)

To check Non-Significant P Value Check

What we found

We found 1 non-significant p value that should be checked for appropriate interpretation.

Show details

Meta-scientific research has shown nonsignificant p values are commonly misinterpreted. It is incorrect to infer that there is ‘no effect’, ‘no difference’, or that groups are ‘the same’ after p > 0.05.

It is possible that there is a true non-zero effect, but that the study did not detect it. Make sure your inference acknowledges that it is possible that there is a non-zero effect. It is correct to include the effect is ‘not significantly’ different, although this just restates that p > 0.05.

Metacheck does not yet analyze automatically whether sentences which include non-significant p-values are correct, but we recommend manually checking the sentences below for possible misinterpreted non-significant p values.

Text Sentence
p = 0.292 OR 1.80, p = 0.292), and atypical dissociation, associated with benignity only in the AI model (OR 0.07, p = 0.007).

For metascientific articles demonstrating the rate of misinterpretations of non-significant results is high, see:

Aczel B, Palfi B, Szollosi A, Kovacs M, Szaszi B, Szecsi P, Zrubka M, Gronau Q, van den Bergh D, Wagenmakers E (2018). “Quantifying Support for the Null Hypothesis in Psychology: An Empirical Investigation.” Advances in Methods and Practices in Psychological Science, 1(3), 357–366. doi:10.1177/2515245918773742.

Murphy S, Merz R, Reimann L, Fernández A (2025). “Nonsignificance misinterpreted as an effect’s absence in psychology: Prevalence and temporal analyses.” Royal Society Open Science, 12(3), 242167. doi:10.1098/rsos.242167.

For educational material on preventing the misinterpretation of p values, see Improving Your Statistical Inferences.

Absolute Paths

Best programming practice is to use relative file paths (e.g., ‘./files’) instead of absolute file paths (e.g., ‘C://Lakens/project_dir/files’) as these folder names do not exist on other computers. No absolute file paths were found in any of the code files.

Working Directory (setwd)

Best programming practice is to avoid setwd() in analysis code: it hardcodes an assumption about the working directory (often an absolute path on the author’s own machine), so the code breaks when run anywhere else. Keep the working directory as the caller sets it and use relative paths. No setwd() calls were found in any of the code files.

Package Installation (install.packages)

Best programming practice is to avoid install.packages() in analysis code: it installs software on whoever runs the script without asking, which is at minimum disruptive (an unexpected install, network access, a package version the author never tested against) and at worst a security risk if it points at an untrusted repository. Document required packages instead (a README, or a list of them: an renv.lock/DESCRIPTION for R, a requirements.txt for Python). install.packages() calls were found in 8 code files.

Spreadsheet formatting such as colour, merged cells, and blank rows/columns is not preserved when data are read programmatically or exported to CSV. Store data as a plain rectangular table (one header row, one column per variable, no colour-encoded meaning) so it is machine-readable.

Careless Responding

No file could be screened for careless responding.

What this does not cover. Only 0 of 46 data files could be screened: the rest had no detectable multi-item scale block, or too few respondents. Even in a screened file, these checks only look at multi-item rating scales — the only place where a repeated or flat answer pattern is interpretable. Single questions, open text, demographics and any item outside a detected scale block are never examined. A respondent can therefore answer most of a survey carelessly and still not be flagged here, and finding nothing is not evidence that a dataset is free of careless responding.

All details of the Reproducibility Check

This module assesses whether the paper’s code could be run on its data, and — because execute = TRUE — actually ran it. We examined 9 R code files.

Run order

The scripts were ordered by their data dependencies (a script writing a file another reads runs first), source() calls, and numeric filename prefixes.

Order File Runs after Basis
1 01_Performance_Malignancy.R — numeric
2 03_SpiderPlots_AUC.R — numeric
3 04_Combined_Model_Performance.R — numeric
4 05_Selected_Criteria_Model_Performance.R — numeric
5 06_Combined_ClinicPRAME_Model_Performance.R — numeric
6 07_Table1_Descriptive_Statistics.R — numeric
7 08_Ground_Truth_Morphology_Benchmark.R — numeric
8 09_Frequency Comparison Table.R — numeric
9 10_Supplementary_Four_Field_Analysis.R — numeric

File paths

Every data path in the code works in the repository as deposited. The code reads files that are only inside ffgellrich/ai-prame-dermatopathology-v1.0.0.zip, and no script unpacks it. We unpacked it in its folder before the run. So that others can run the code as deposited, start the code with a line that unpacks it (such as unzip("ai-prame-dermatopathology-v1.0.0.zip") in R), or upload the files unpacked.

Execution

The code was run. Each script ran in an isolated Docker container against a throwaway copy of the repository, in the run order above, with a 300-second per-script timeout. Of 9 scripts: 9 ran without error, 0 errored, 0 timed out, 0 could not run because one of its own dependencies is unavailable, 0 did not parse. Running against current package versions: a break can reflect version drift, which argues for pinning versions.

>   ci_val  <- pROC::ci.auc(roc_obj, method = "delong")
>   
>   tibble(N = nrow(clean), AUC = as.numeric(roc_obj$auc), Low = ci_val[1], High = ci_val[3])
> }

> get_cat_row <- function(data, var_name, label, show_missing = TRUE) {
>   sub <- data %>% select(Set, val = !!sym(var_name)) %>% mutate(val = as.character(val))
>   if(show_missing) sub$val[is.na(sub$val)] <- "Missing / Unknown" else sub <- sub %>% filter(!is.na(val))
>   if(nrow(sub) == 0) return(tibble(Characteristic = label, `Training Set` = "0 (0.0%)", `Test Set` = "0 (0.0%)", p_val_raw = NA))
>   tab <- table(sub$Set, sub$val)
>   p_val <- if(ncol(tab) > 1 && nrow(tab) > 1) suppressWarnings(chisq.test(tab)$p.value) else NA
>   lvls <- sort(unique(sub$val))
>   if("Missing / Unknown" %in% lvls) lvls <- c(lvls[lvls != "Missing / Unknown"], "Missing / Unknown")
>   summary_stats <- sub %>% group_by(Set, val) %>% tally() %>% group_by(Set) %>% 
>     mutate(perc = (n / sum(n)) * 100, text = sprintf("%d (%.1f%%)", n, perc))
>   res_list <- lapply(lvls, function(lvl) {
>     tibble(Characteristic = paste0("  ", lvl),
>            `Training Set` = summary_stats$text[summary_stats$Set == "Training Set (Historical 80%)" & summary_stats$val == lvl] %||% "0 (0.0%)",
>            `Test Set` = summary_stats$text[summary_stats$Set == "Independent Test Set (Most Recent 20%)" & summary_stats$val == lvl] %||% "0 (0.0%)",
>            p_val_raw = NA)
>   })
>   bind_rows(tibble(Characteristic = label, `Training Set` = "", `Test Set` = "", p_val_raw = p_val), bind_rows(res_list))
> }
> get_binary_row <- function(data, var_name, label) {
>   sub <- data %>% select(Set, val = !!sym(var_name)) %>% mutate(val = tolower(as.character(val))) %>% filter(!is.na(val))
>   tab <- table(sub$Set, sub$val)
>   p_val <- if(ncol(tab) > 1 && nrow(tab) > 1) suppressWarnings(chisq.test(tab)$p.value) else NA
>   stats <- sub %>% group_by(Set) %>% summarise(n_total = n(), n_ja = sum(val == "ja", na.rm = TRUE), perc = (n_ja / n_total) * 100, text = sprintf("%d/%d (%.1f%%)", n_ja, n_total, perc))
>   tibble(Characteristic = label, 
>          `Training Set` = stats$text[stats$Set == "Training Set (Historical 80%)"] %||% "0/0 (0.0%)",
>          `Test Set` = stats$text[stats$Set == "Independent Test Set (Most Recent 20%)"] %||% "0/0 (0.0%)",
>          p_val_raw = p_val)
> }
> get_binary_subcohort_row <- function(data, var_name, label) {

>   p_val <- if("yes" %in% sub$val && ncol(tab) > 1 && nrow(tab) > 1) suppressWarnings(chisq.test(tab)$p.value) else NA
>   stats <- sub %>% group_by(Set) %>% 
>     summarise(
>       n_total = n(), 
>       n_ja = sum(val == "yes", na.rm = TRUE), 
>       perc = (n_ja / n_total) * 100, 
>       text = sprintf("%d (%.1f%%)", n_ja, perc),
>       .groups = "drop"
>     )
>   tibble(Characteristic = paste0("    ", label), 
>          `Training Set` = stats$text[stats$Set == "Training Set (Historical 80%)"] %||% "0 (0.0%)",
>          `Test Set` = stats$text[stats$Set == "Independent Test Set (Most Recent 20%)"] %||% "0 (0.0%)",
>          p_val_raw = p_val)
> }
> get_na_row <- function(data, var_name, label) {

>     )

>          p_val_raw = NA)
> }

> full_legend <- "Note: The study cohort was partitioned using a chronological (historical) split, with the most recent 20% of cases assigned to an independent test set. Continuous variables are reported as Median [Interquartile Range (IQR)]; categorical variables are reported as N (%). P-values were determined using the Wilcoxon rank-sum test for continuous data and Chi-square or Fisher's exact tests for categorical data. To control for type I error accumulation, multiple testing adjustments were performed using the Benjamini-Hochberg (False Discovery Rate, FDR) procedure, applied strictly and independently within each individual class of hypotheses (the nevus subclassification family, the melanoma in situ subclassification family, and the group of 18 morphological criteria, respectively). 'Corrected Diagnosis (Slide-level)' refers to a retrospective histopathological re-evaluation of the specific slide used for AI analysis, noting that in some cases only in situ components were present despite a case-level diagnosis of invasive melanoma. Subclassification percentages for nevi, melanomas in situ, and invasive parameters are calculated relative to their respective main diagnostic categories and may exceed 100% due to overlapping clinicopathological features. Bold p-values indicate statistical significance (p < 0.05 after class-wise FDR adjustment)."

>   "Pagetoide_Durchsetzung" = "Pagetoid Spread", "Konfluenz_junktionaler_Nester" = "Nest Confluence",
>   "Ausgepraegte_junktionale_Atypien" = "Junctional Atypia", "Atypische_junktionale_Mitosen" = "Junctional Mitoses",
>   "Fehlende_Ausreifung_in_Nestern" = "Lack of Maturation", "Ausgepraegte_dermale_Atypien" = "Dermal Atypia",
>   "Dermale_Mitosen" = "Dermal Mitoses", "Geordnete_Vereinzelung_Benignes_Muster" = "Ordered Single Cells",
>   "Atypische_Vereinzelung_Dissoziation_Malignes_Muster" = "Atypical Dissociation",
>   "Regression" = "Regression", "Ulzeration" = "Ulceration",
>   "Junktionale_Beteiligung" = "Junctional Component", "Dermale_Beteiligung" = "Dermal Component",
>   "Dichtes_lymphozytaeres_Infiltrat" = "Dense Lymphocytic Infiltrate",
>   "Intratumorales_lymphozytaeres_Infiltrat_TILs" = "Tumor-Infiltrating Lymphocytes", 
>   "Infiltration_der_Subkutis" = "Subcutis Infiltration"
> )
> get_agreement_table <- function(train_data, test_data, target_set = "train") {
>   data <- if(target_set == "train") train_data else test_data
>   n_total <- nrow(data)
>   results <- list()
>   
>   # A. Morphological Criteria (Calibrated Prediction)
>   for(orig in names(morph_map)) {
>     eng <- morph_map[orig]
>     gt_col <- paste0(orig, "_GroundTruth"); score_col <- paste0(orig, "_ja")
>     
>     train_temp <- train_data %>%
>       mutate(y = ifelse(!!sym(gt_col) %in% c("ja", 1), 1, 0)) %>%
>       select(y, score = !!sym(score_col)) %>% drop_na()
>     fit <- glm(y ~ score, data = train_temp, family = binomial)
>     
>     data_temp <- data %>%
>       mutate(gt_pos = !!sym(gt_col) %in% c("ja", 1)) %>%
>       select(gt_pos, score = !!sym(score_col))
>     data_temp$ai_pos <- predict(fit, newdata = data_temp, type = "response") > 0.5
>     
>     tp <- sum(data_temp$gt_pos & data_temp$ai_pos, na.rm = TRUE)
>     fn <- sum(data_temp$gt_pos & !data_temp$ai_pos, na.rm = TRUE)
>     fp <- sum(!data_temp$gt_pos & data_temp$ai_pos, na.rm = TRUE)
>     tn <- sum(!data_temp$gt_pos & !data_temp$ai_pos, na.rm = TRUE)
>     
>     results[[eng]] <- tibble(
>       Criterion = eng,
>       col_tp = sprintf("%d (%.1f%%)", tp, (tp/n_total)*100),
>       col_fn = sprintf("%d (%.1f%%)", fn, (fn/n_total)*100),
>       col_fp = sprintf("%d (%.1f%%)", fp, (fp/n_total)*100),
>       col_tn = sprintf("%d (%.1f%%)", tn, (tn/n_total)*100),
>       `Total Human GT` = sprintf("%d (%.1f%%)", (tp+fn), ((tp+fn)/n_total)*100),
>       `Total AI Pred`  = sprintf("%d (%.1f%%)", (tp+fp), ((tp+fp)/n_total)*100)
>     )
>   }
>   
>   # B. PRAME Status
>   for(v in 0:4) {
>     gt_vec <- data$PRAME_Status_GroundTruth == v
>     ai_vec <- data$PRAME_Status_pred == v
>     tp <- sum(gt_vec & ai_vec, na.rm = TRUE); fn <- sum(gt_vec & !ai_vec, na.rm = TRUE)
>     fp <- sum(!gt_vec & ai_vec, na.rm = TRUE); tn <- sum(!gt_vec & !ai_vec, na.rm = TRUE)
>     name <- paste0("PRAME Status: ", v)
>     results[[name]] <- tibble(
>       Criterion = name, col_tp = sprintf("%d (%.1f%%)", tp, (tp/n_total)*100),
>       col_fn = sprintf("%d (%.1f%%)", fn, (fn/n_total)*100), col_fp = sprintf("%d (%.1f%%)", fp, (fp/n_total)*100),
>       col_tn = sprintf("%d (%.1f%%)", tn, (tn/n_total)*100),
>       `Total Human GT` = sprintf("%d (%.1f%%)", (tp+fn), ((tp+fn)/n_total)*100),
>       `Total AI Pred`  = sprintf("%d (%.1f%%)", (tp+fp), ((tp+fp)/n_total)*100)
>     )
>   }
>   
>   # C. Ki-67 (Specific denominator based on available data)
>   mib_map <- c("Niedrig" = "Low", "Intermediaer" = "Intermediate", "Hoch" = "High")
>   n_mib_available <- sum(!is.na(data$Mib1_GroundTruth))
>   
>   for(orig_m in names(mib_map)) {
>     eng_m <- mib_map[orig_m]
>     gt_vec <- str_detect(as.character(data$Mib1_GroundTruth), orig_m)
>     ai_vec <- str_detect(as.character(data$Mib1_pred), orig_m)
>     tp <- sum(gt_vec & ai_vec, na.rm = TRUE); fn <- sum(gt_vec & !ai_vec, na.rm = TRUE)
>     fp <- sum(!gt_vec & ai_vec, na.rm = TRUE); tn <- sum(!gt_vec & !ai_vec, na.rm = TRUE)
>     
>     name <- paste0("Ki-67 Index: ", eng_m)
>     results[[name]] <- tibble(
>       Criterion = name,
>       col_tp = sprintf("%d (%.1f%%)", tp, (tp/n_mib_available)*100),
>       col_fn = sprintf("%d (%.1f%%)", fn, (fn/n_mib_available)*100),
>       col_fp = sprintf("%d (%.1f%%)", fp, (fp/n_mib_available)*100),
>       col_tn = sprintf("%d (%.1f%%)", tn, (tn/n_mib_available)*100),
>       `Total Human GT` = sprintf("%d (%.1f%%)", (tp+fn), ((tp+fn)/n_mib_available)*100),
>       `Total AI Pred`  = sprintf("%d (%.1f%%)", (tp+fp), ((tp+fp)/n_mib_available)*100)
>     )
>   }
>   return(bind_rows(results))
> }
> ft_formatted <- function(df, title) {
>   legend_text <- "Note: Confusion matrix of human-AI agreement. TP (True Positive) and TN (True Negative) indicate consensus; FN (False Negative) represents features identified by humans only; FP (False Positive) represents features identified by AI only. Marginal totals (Total Human GT / Total AI Pred) provide the overall frequency of feature detection. AI classifications for morphological criteria were optimized via probability-calibrated logistic regression models. Percentages for Ki-67 reflect only evaluable cases."
>   
>   flextable(df) %>%
>     set_caption(title) %>% theme_vanilla() %>% autofit() %>%
>     bold(part = "header") %>% bold(j = 1, part = "body") %>%
>     align(j = 2:7, align = "center", part = "all") %>%
>     set_header_labels(col_tp = "Agreement Both (TP)", col_fn = "Human only (FN)", col_fp = "AI only (FP)", col_tn = "Agreement Both (TN)",
>                       `Total Human GT` = "Total Human GT (+)", `Total AI Pred` = "Total AI Pred (+)") %>%
>     add_footer_lines(legend_text) %>%
>     bg(j = 6:7, bg = "#F2F2F2", part = "all")
> }
> tab_cv80     <- get_agreement_table(df_train, df_test, "train")
> tab_deploy20 <- get_agreement_table(df_train, df_test, "test")
> doc <- read_docx() %>%
>   body_add_par("Supplementary Material: Human-AI Agreement Analysis", style = "heading 1") %>%
>   body_add_flextable(ft_formatted(tab_cv80, "Supplementary Table S3: Agreement Matrix (Training Set, N=800)")) %>% body_add_break() %>%
>   body_add_flextable(ft_formatted(tab_deploy20, "Supplementary Table S4: Agreement Matrix (Independent Test Set, N=200)")) %>%
>   body_end_section_landscape()
> print(doc, target = file.path(table_dir, "10_Supplementary_Four_Field_Agreement.docx"))
> dir.create(csv_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
> write_csv(tab_cv80, file.path(csv_dir, "10_Agreement_Analysis_Training_Set.csv"))
> write_csv(tab_deploy20, file.path(csv_dir, "10_Agreement_Analysis_Test_Set.csv"))
> cat("\n--- Script 10 (Supplementary Four Field Analysis) successfully executed. ---\n")

Python code

This module also assesses whether the paper’s Python code could be run on its data, and — because execute = TRUE — actually ran it. We examined 1 Python code file.

Run order

The scripts were ordered by their data dependencies (a script writing a file another reads runs first) and numeric filename prefixes. Python has no source()-equivalent import-based ordering signal (an import loads a module, not the paper’s own analysis flow), so that basis never applies here.

Order File Runs after Basis
1 generate_single_script.py — none

File paths

Every data path in the code works in the repository as deposited. The code reads files that are only inside ffgellrich/ai-prame-dermatopathology-v1.0.0.zip, and no script unpacks it. We unpacked it in its folder before the run. So that others can run the code as deposited, start the code with a line that unpacks it (such as zipfile.ZipFile("ai-prame-dermatopathology-v1.0.0.zip").extractall() in Python), or upload the files unpacked.

Execution

The Python code was run. Each script ran in an isolated Docker container against a throwaway copy of the repository, in the run order above, with a 300-second per-script timeout. Of 1 script: 1 ran without error, 0 errored, 0 timed out, 0 could not run because one of its own dependencies is unavailable, 0 did not parse, and 0 are written for Python 2 and not run. Running against current package versions: a break can reflect version drift, which argues for pinning versions (e.g. in a requirements.txt).
